title: lint: an overlay write (no package) of a list view bound to an object that exists nowhere answers 200 with no issue — `validateListViewFieldRefs` skips it and no other rule judges a `view` write's binding
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named locus.** The declared contract is #24563's: the standalone list-view door "reaches the author who made the typo". It does not hold on the overlay door for the binding itself. Reader: the `domain:spec` seat, in `packages/lint`. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549), session `session_019oFY6Hi35J7atvgVFnmoaK`, from out-of-scope finding (a) of PR #24630. The contract review `6278531343` judged it class a. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Measured

- `packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`, at PR #24630's head `700c21cbbd` (lines 823–826):

  ```ts
  if (!graph.has(object)) {
    if (scope) reportOutsideClosure(scope, object, where, bindingPath);
    return;
  }
  ```

  With no package closure stated (an overlay write, or the CLI), an unresolvable binding returns silently. At the merge base `c3954057fe` it is the single skip at line 710.
- `packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts:224`: `validateObjectReferences` runs on `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'dataset']`, never on a `view` write. So no rule judges a `view` write's binding against the object collection.
- The #24563 dev measured it through `saveMetaItem` over the stub engine. An overlay write (no `?package=`) of a list view bound to `nosuch_obj` answers success with `advisories: []`. PR #24630 pins this as **unchanged** (its protocol case (c) and the lint "a write that names no package" case), deliberately, because it was out of that card's scope.
- **Not measured:** the booted HTTP door. The first step is that reading: `PUT /api/v1/meta/view/:name` with no `?package=` and `data.object: 'nosuch_obj'`.

## Why it matters

A view bound to a misspelled or deleted object is stored, and fails only at render. #24563's changeset says such a view fails at render with "This view's query was rejected". Under a package closure, PR #24630 now refuses the same body (`list-view-object-outside-closure`). The overlay door and `os validate` still say nothing.

## Shape of a fix (not decided here)

The skip-1 rationale in the module docblock is: there, an unresolved binding may come from another package, and `defineStack` / `validateObjectReferences` own it. Neither owns it on a `view` write. The options:
- extend `validateObjectReferences`'s `runtimeTypes` to `view` for the binding key;
- or have the overlay door judge the binding against the whole collection, where "exists nowhere" is decidable.

Clause-②: a narrowing, so it falls under the protocol-class 「是否提前」 rule (`6261447528`).

## Dedupe

I ran a semantic issue search for `overlay list view bound to nonexistent object accepted save door view data.object unresolved no advisory`. It returned 19 hits. The relevant one is #24563, the in-closure half that PR #24630 fixes. None covers the overlay door.
